# Ridu 0.16.0

REST and the SDK now send the error codes the documentation describes, typed Go handles can publish
versioned content, and data transforms read the collection shapes their own migration defines. The
migrations and work-with-data documentation is rewritten around tasks, diagrams, and side-by-side
Go, TypeScript, and REST examples.

## Changes

- REST and the SDK send `bad_query` (400) for a filter, sort, selection, or population the
  collection can't run, and `publish_required` (409) for a plain update of a published versioned
  document or global. Both used to arrive as `bad_request`.
- Any other error reports the code its status names: `access_denied` for 403, `not_found` for 404,
  `conflict` for 409, `bad_request` for other 4xx statuses, and `internal` for 5xx. A 404 for an
  unknown collection no longer says `bad_request`.
- `RequestObservation.ErrorReason` holds the specific code behind the public one, such as
  `origin_denied` behind `access_denied` or `body_too_large` behind `bad_request`, for monitoring
  and alerts.
- Generated typed collection handles gain `Publish`, `PublishChanges`, and `Unpublish`, and typed
  global handles gain `PublishChanges`. Typed code can now edit a published versioned document
  without falling back to `store.Values`.
- `migration.DataTransaction` gains `Collection` and `Global`, which return a resource as the
  running migration leaves it, or its earlier shape when the migration removes it. Transforms that
  resolved the current config broke `ridu migrate verify` and new databases once a later migration
  changed the collection.
- The SDK's `auth.createUser` resolves to the user type when the session collection has no drafts,
  instead of `Promise<never>`, and rejects incomplete data and `{ draft: true }` there.
- SQLite reports that a database file's directory doesn't exist, instead of only
  "SQLite error 14". Other SQLite errors include the driver's description of their code.
- Inside Claude Code, `ridu new` and `ridu agent install` default to the Claude layout
  (`CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills`), and the wizard preselects it. An explicit `--agent` or
  `--no-agent` still wins, and other environments keep the Codex default.
- The `ridu-project` skill no longer tells agents to pass `--allow-maintenance` to
  `ridu migrate verify`; only `ridu migrate up` needs it.
- The migrations documentation is a short overview with diagrams and seven task pages. Querying
  data, the Local Go API, and the TypeScript SDK are split into task pages with a new Writing data
  page, and a reader's choice of code tab carries across examples and pages.

## Breaking changes and upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.16.0 together, regenerate application contracts,
and rebuild the admin and application binary. Migration planners and database layouts are unchanged
from 0.15.0, so existing databases and migration histories need no recreation.

- REST clients and SDK code that matched `bad_request` now receive `bad_query` for refused queries,
  `publish_required` for an update that needs publishing, and `access_denied`, `not_found`, or
  `conflict` for 403, 404, and 409 responses. The SDK's `ErrorCode` type includes `bad_query` and
  `publish_required`.
- Alerts that need the specific cause of a rejection, such as `origin_denied`, `host_denied`, or
  `body_too_large`, should read `RequestObservation.ErrorReason`. `ErrorCode` carries only the
  public code.
- Go types that implement `migration.DataTransaction`, such as test doubles, must add `Collection`
  and `Global`.

Enabling versioning on an already populated unversioned resource remains unsupported. This is a
pre-1 release with breaking contracts; keep the coordinated packages aligned. Production still runs
as a Go binary with its static admin embedded, without a JavaScript server.
